name: phpggc
summary: A library of PHP unserialize() payloads along with a tool to generate them, from command line or programmatically.
highlights: -i — Displays information about a gadget chain
-o — Outputs the payload to a file instead of standard output
-p — Creates a PHAR file of the given format
-pj — Creates a polyglot JPEG/PHAR file from given image
-pp — Sets the PHAR prefix as the contents of the given file. Generally used with -p phar to con
-pf — Defines the name of the file contained in the generated PHAR (default: test.txt)
-f — Applies the fast-destruct technique, so that the object is destroyed right after the unser
-a — Uses the 'S' serialization format instead of the standard 's' for non-printable chars. Thi

flags.name: --information
flags.description: Displays information about a gadget chain

flags.name: --output
flags.description: Outputs the payload to a file instead of standard output

flags.name: --phar
flags.description: Creates a PHAR file of the given format

flags.name: --phar-jpeg
flags.description: Creates a polyglot JPEG/PHAR file from given image

flags.name: --phar-prefix
flags.description: Sets the PHAR prefix as the contents of the given file. Generally used with -p phar to control the beginning of the generated file.

flags.name: --phar-filename
flags.description: Defines the name of the file contained in the generated PHAR (default: test.txt)

flags.name: --fast-destruct
flags.description: Applies the fast-destruct technique, so that the object is destroyed right after the unserialize() call, as opposed to at the end of the script

flags.name: --ascii-strings
flags.description: Uses the 'S' serialization format instead of the standard 's' for non-printable chars. This replaces every non-ASCII value to an hexadecimal representation: s:5:"A<null_byte>B<cr><lf>"; -> S:5:"A\00B\09\0D"; This is experimental and it might not work in some cases.

flags.name: --armor-strings
flags.description: Uses the 'S' serialization format instead of the standard 's' for every char. This replaces every character to an hexadecimal representation: s:5:"A<null_byte>B<cr><lf>"; -> S:5:"\41\00\42\09\0D"; This is experimental and it might not work in some cases. Note: Since strings grow by a factor of 3 using this option, the payload can get really long.

flags.name: --plus-numbers
flags.description: Adds a + symbol in front of every number symbol of the given type. For instance, -n iO adds a + in front of every int and object name size: O:3:"Abc":1:{s:1:"x";i:3;} -> O:+3:"Abc":1:{s:1:"x";i:+3;} Note: Since PHP 7.2, only i and d (float) types can have a +

flags.name: --wrapper
flags.description: Specifies a file containing at least one wrapper functions: - process_parameters(array $parameters): called right before object is created - process_object(object $object): called right before the payload is serialized - process_serialized(string $serialized): called right after the payload is serialized

flags.name: --test-payload
flags.description: Instead of displaying or storing the payload, includes vendor/autoload.php and unserializes the payload. The test script can only deserialize __destruct, __wakeup, __toString and PHAR payloads. Warning: This will run the payload on YOUR system !
